newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar turns lower, focus on July-Oct.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar turns lower, focus on July-Oct.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures dipped back below unchanged in late morning after setting new contract highs early Friday as the July-October spread came under renewed selling pressure.

World sugar prices see-sawed from the opening, falling to the lows early before end-users stepped in to buy. Shortcovering by day traders helped nudge the market toward even, stirring up interest from commodity funds.
But persistent selling against the nearby switch knocked the market back down by late morning, dealers said.
"The market is encountering resistance from July-October selling," said one broker. "Some of the spec buying just dried up and some locals are getting out of their longs."

Benchmark October futures stood at 11.29 cents a lb as of 1112 EDT, off 0.05 cent from Thursday's close and below a new contract high of 11.40 cents. Spot July was 0.11 lower at 11.38, traded 11.51 to 11.35.
Fresh fundamentals were scarce this morning, but traders said signs of steady physical offtake in the past few weeks should continue to underpin the raws market.

Technically, traders kept their eyes on the 11.58-mark basis July, a contract high reached on June 4. Few fireworks were expected from today's July options expiry, though the widely-held 11.00 cent strike price could exert some downward pressure before the day's end, dealers said.
An estimated 16,376 lots were exchanged as of 1100 EDT.
(( W Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640))
